status: Vehicle and crew filled from public sources, re-cited after the October 2026 research review (docs/research/OSA_RESEARCH_2026-10.md). Radar and missile sections stay empty: outcomes come from the gameplay-level model (data/gameplay/osa_ak.json), not from per-system performance data. No value cites a tier-5 source (roadmap 6.8; tools/check_citations.py checks it).

crew.notes: An officer; receives target designations from the battery PU-12 by radio and gives orders. NVA: the platoon leader commands one of the platoon's vehicles. Front cab, beside the driver (zbiam_2019).

Soviet staffing decision (1971, korovin_tiv_2010): a conscript sergeant, later a warrant officer (прапорщик), instead of a second officer. NVA: career NCO. Deputy crew chief: launch console (key, launch-ready lamp, missile selector, voltmeter), elevation wheel, TV monitor, elevation display. SAM Simulator: Firing Officer / elevation operator. wrk: guidance operator.
Search radar scope, IFF interrogation, puts the target under the azimuth and range marks with handwheels. SAM Simulator: azimuth operator. wrk: search operator.
Range display and range tracking; captures with ТСЦ. SAM Simulator: Range Officer. wrk: range operator.

Crew of five in the NVA (flak11), Soviet (wrk), Polish and ru_wiki sources for the Osa-AK, and in voenizdat_osa_1991 p17 for the Osa-AKM (crew chief; guidance, search and range operators; driver-mechanic-electrician). Four in Russian service after the Osa-AKM1 upgrade ('crew reduced by one', nvo_2015; ilya_prosto).

max_road_speed_mps.source: mon_2112_80 p11 (Polish Osa-AK manual: road 60 km/h, dirt roads 30, cross-country 10, water 8 km/h), wrk (60 km/h)
max_road_speed_mps.notes: Sources disagree: 60 km/h (the Polish operator's manual for exactly the Osa-AK, and wrk), 70 km/h (flak11 for the 9A33BM2, ru_wiki; flak11 adds 'in practice much faster'), 80 km/h (korovin_tiv_2010 for the original 9A33B; nuou; wrk for the chassis). The official 60 km/h is used. Dirt-road averages 36 km/h by day, 25 km/h at night (korovin_tiv_2010).

deploy_time_s.source: mon_2112_80 p11–12 (march to combat at most 4 min, including starting the gas-turbine generator), voenizdat_osa_1991 p16 (the same 4 min for the Osa-AKM), nvo_2015, wrk
deploy_time_s.notes: Russian norms quoted as 3 min for the Osa-AKM. voenizdat_osa_1991 p231 gives 35–50 s for the battery into combat order and 15–30 s back to march order (from a powered march; video_osa said the same). Different measure: a cold start (switch-on cycle 3.8 min + function check 3.0 min = 6.8 min, flak11 9K33-0), which SAM3D does not model yet (roadmap 6.2). The Polish manual allows at most 10 min for the function check (mon_2112_80 p19). SAM3D's crew reaches search after about 4 min: GTA start (60 s, estimate) and the equipment's 3 min (voenizdat_osa_1991 p53, p165).

stow_time_s.source: ru_wiki (deployment and stowing not more than 5 min)
stow_time_s.notes: No tier-1 source for stowing a single vehicle from cold; voenizdat_osa_1991 p231 gives a battery 15–30 s back into march order from a powered halt.

search_on_the_move_max_speed_mps.source: wrk (search possible at up to 80 km/h)

engages_from.source: nvo_2015 ('с места или короткой остановки'), wrk, flak11

power.value: 9И120 gas-turbine unit (on the move and at a halt); engine power take-off generator (at a halt only)
power.source: vpvo, wrk, samsim_thread (ePap); mon_2112_80 p20, p27 (also an external supply at a halt); voenizdat_osa_1991 p163–164 (50 kW at 67 kg/h of fuel; 35 kW at 20 kg/h)
power.notes: 9И120 = 9И56-3 gas-turbine engine + С-75 generator, 50 kW; the take-off generator 35 kW, at a halt only. Fuel (ePap): ~300 l tank, turbine ~75 l/h stationary and ~100 l/h moving, take-off generator ~25 l/h; half the tank is kept for driving. voenizdat_osa_1991 p163-164 gives 67 kg/h (about 80 l/h) and 20 kg/h (about 24 l/h); p17, p231: 250 km on the fuel with 2 h of the turbine, 500 km with the fuel the TZM carries, at most 70 l per 100 km on roads; 48 h of continuous work with refuelling. '9I210' in apa and flak11 is probably a confusion with the 9В210 maintenance vehicle.

validation_scenarios.description: Training-range shoot (Ashuluk, Kapustin Yar, Ustka, NAMFI style): drones or P-15 targets, two-missile salvo, a kill near maximum range (10.3 km reported at Kapustin Yar, 2013)
Bekaa, 24 July 1982: Syrian SA-8 shoots down an Israeli F-4E while other vehicles are attacked
Cuito Cuanavale, 1987–88: FAPLA Osa-AK units against SAAF aircraft and RPVs; Mirage F1AZ, 20 February 1988
